original_value: Sea ice leads (fractures) play a critical role in the exchange of mass and energy between the ocean and atmosphere in the polar regions. The thinning of Arctic sea ice over the last few decades will likely result in changes in lead distributions, so monitoring their characteristics is increasingly important. Here we present a methodology to detect and characterize sea ice leads using satellite imager thermal infrared window channels. A thermal contrast method is first used to identify possible sea ice lead pixels, then a number of geometric and image analysis tests are applied to build a subset of positively identified leads. Finally, characteristics such as width, length and orientation are derived. This methodology is applied to Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) observations for the months of January through April over the period of 2003 to 2018. The algorithm results are compared to other satellite estimates of lead distribution. Lead coverage maps and statistics over the Arctic illustrate spatial and temporal lead patterns.

result.paraphrase: Sea ice leads, or fractures, are crucial for mass and energy exchange between the ocean and atmosphere in polar regions. As Arctic sea ice has thinned over recent decades, lead distributions are likely to change, making it increasingly important to monitor their properties. Here, we describe a method for detecting and characterizing sea ice leads with satellite imager thermal infrared window channels. It first applies a thermal contrast approach to flag potential lead pixels, then uses several geometric and image-analysis tests to form a subset of confirmed leads. Lastly, it derives properties including width, length, and orientation. The method is applied to Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) observations from January to April during 2003–2018. The algorithm outputs are compared with other satellite estimates of lead distribution. Lead coverage maps and statistics across the Arctic show spatial and seasonal lead patterns.
